approach: Part (1) is already done in the base: model.json:10 has `reopened` as kind "waiting", model.json:110 has t12 reopened -> queued, intro.json:54 (lead-in) and :115 (glossary) say only Done ends the task and reopened goes back to Queued, and claims.json c45 (:345-350) is cited by both. CHANGELOG.md:987 and HISTORY.txt:633 (commit 30642c0) record it. So the study files are left unedited, except that claim c45's citation is corrected if the pinned source shows it wrong. That claim cites bin/fm-teardown.sh lines 3894-3896 with the quote "Queued", while every other citation of that file is at line 184 or earlier. The real work is part (2). In steward.rs, add a `SourceFinding` type (file, kind, text) and `source_fix_request`, which builds one request through `StewardRequest::new`. Each finding contributes one stable marker line `Source finding: <file> (<kind>)` plus its full checker text (statement and cited source). Also add `open_requests` (every request job whose state is not Closed) and `citing_request`, which matches an open request by the marker line only. The marker is the study file and kind, never the model's wording, so a reworded finding does not queue again (review finding 4). In drain.rs, `Check` carries `findings`. `RealSteps::check_page` builds them from the model-free floor and from the checker's problem strings, parsed by a pure function `source_findings` that accepts only the `<study>/<file>: <kind> statement "..." (...)` shape pin.rs:489-492 produces. Infrastructure problems (checker did not run, file not read, unreadable study, invalid JSON) stay in `held_back` only. Two `Steps` hooks, `open_requests` and `queue_request`, have inert defaults. `RealSteps` implements them with `steward::open_requests` over `Records` and `Athena::queue` (reading.rs:919), the call code_health.rs:763 uses for its own StewardRequest text. `Athena::queue` already refuses banned input, redacts the text and commits 'Queue a request: <title>', so no new commit helper is needed (finding 6). `Drain::rate` calls `queue_source_fix` on a failed check, under the landing lock it already holds. It filters out the findings an open request cites, queues one request for the rest, and notes either the queued job or, for a skipped finding, the citing request's id and state (finding 8). pin.rs, refusal_corpus.rs and any change to the checker call are not touched (findings 1 and 3); tests/drain.rs gets one added integration test, because it is the only place the real checker output meets the real queue (finding 2).

decisions.choice: Do not edit pin.rs. Build findings in drain.rs from the existing problem strings with a pure function `source_findings(study, problems)`, which accepts only strings of the exact shape pin.rs:489-492 formats (`<study>/<file>: <kind> statement "…" (…)`, kind one of contradicted, omitted, behavior). The finding's text is everything after `<kind> statement`, so statement and cited source stay together unsplit.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 1 and 4 together. pin.rs is not a deliverable. The key is only file and kind, so the parse never has to split a statement from its evidence, which could itself hold `" (`. A problem that does not match (`the checker did not report reading this file`, `the text could not be checked`) is left out and stays in held_back.

rejected.why: Widens scope beyond the listed files (review finding 1). The shape is covered by the new real-checker test in tests/drain.rs, which fails if pin.rs changes its format.

rejected.option: Split the statement from the evidence with a regex
rejected.why: Breaks when either holds `" (` and gains nothing, since the whole text is cited.

decisions.choice: The dedupe key is a marker line `Source finding: <study file path> (<kind>)` written into the request body. A finding counts as cited when a non-Closed request job holds that exact line (trimmed). The statement and evidence wording are never compared. The marker passes through `plain_boundary_text`, like the body, before it is compared. Several findings in one file and kind share one marker.
decisions.reason: Review finding 4: for `omitted` the statement is the model's own words (pin.rs:346-347) and for `behavior` it is a span the model picks (pin.rs:352), so it varies run to run. File and kind stay the same while the same fault persists. The trade-off: while a fix request for `studies/x/model.json (behavior)` is open, a second distinct behavior finding in that file is not queued. It is queued on the first drain after the request closes if still present, and the drain note says it is held by that open request.

rejected.option: Key on the exact statement text
rejected.why: Not stable for omitted and behavior findings, so the same fault would be queued on every drain, which is the defect to fix.
Still fails when the model rewords the fact; it only handles trivial variation and adds a matcher to maintain.

rejected.option: Treat any open source-fix request as covering every finding
rejected.why: Hides a finding in a different file or kind for as long as any fix request is open.

decisions.choice: Queue through `Athena::queue(text)` with text from `StewardRequest::render()`. Put the builder, `SourceFinding`, `OpenRequest`, `open_requests` and `citing_request` in steward.rs. Add no commit helper.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 6. `Athena::queue` (reading.rs:919-949) calls refuse_banned_input, redacts the text, picks a fresh job id and commits the request record with the Athena-Job trailer, exactly what code_health.rs:763 does with its StewardRequest text. The channel is `cli`, one of DRAINED_CHANNELS (steward.rs:342), so the drain works it. The request carries `Priority: high`.

rejected.option: A new `queue_steward_request` in steward.rs that writes a Request on the steward channel
rejected.why: Duplicates Athena::queue, skips redaction, and adds a second commit path.

decisions.choice: `open` means any request job whose state is not Closed (Queued, Proposed, Declined, Dispatched, Blocked). The drain note names the citing request's id and state whenever a finding is skipped. A statement is quoted inside the request, as pin.rs already formats it (`statement "…"`).
decisions.reason: A running or blocked fix is still an open fix. A stuck request (declined, blocked) shows in the note and in `athena status`, and the person can close it, after which the next drain queues a new one (finding 8). Quoted statements take the 'structural-term-quoted-or-cited' path, covered by the existing case `structural-term-quoted-or-cited-mentions-are-accepted` (refusal_corpus.rs:1316).

rejected.option: Count only Queued/Proposed jobs as open (as `improvement_requests`, steward.rs:376, does)
rejected.why: A running fix job would be duplicated on the next drain.

No reading or admission rule changes; the corpus tests those rules, and refusal_corpus.rs is not a deliverable (finding 3). A steward.rs unit test builds a request from a statement with a structural term and checks it with `request_text_acceptance`; the corpus test is run as a regression.

decisions.choice: Queue findings only for what the page says wrong: the checker's contradicted, omitted and behavior problems, and the model-free floor's `model_contradictions` (file model.json, kind `model-contradiction`). Everything else is held-back text only. One request per failed check, at most 10 findings; findings left over are uncited, so a later drain picks them up.
decisions.reason: A checker timeout or an unreadable study is not a content fix. One request per failed check is the 'queue one fix request' acceptance. The cap keeps the request text bounded.

rejected.why: Contradicts 'one fix request' and floods the queue.

rejected.option: Queue a request for infrastructure problems
rejected.why: There is no page statement to cite, and the request would repeat every drain.

risks.risk: Claim c45's cited lines (bin/fm-teardown.sh 3894-3896, quote 'Queued') may not exist at the pinned commit, since every other citation of that file is at line 184 or earlier. The live drain source check could then keep failing on the study. This plan cannot check it because pinned-source/ is absent here.
risks.mitigation: The criterion 3 host step runs the cap-study validation test, which checks every citation without a model call, and corrects c45 if it fails. If the fault stays, the new drain behavior queues one fix request for it, which is the behavior being added.

risks.risk: The coarse key (study file and kind) holds back a second distinct finding in the same file and kind while one fix request is open.
risks.mitigation: Intended trade-off for stability: it is queued on the first drain after the open request closes, and the note names the holding request's id and state. Findings in other files or kinds are not held.

risks.risk: A fix request that is declined or blocked stays open and so blocks re-queueing, and a request whose job fails and closes is replaced by a new one on the next drain, one per drain.
risks.mitigation: Every skip notes the holding request's id and state, so a stuck request is visible. A closed request is no longer open by design, so a failed fix is retried at one request per drain; one request per failed check and the 10-finding cap bound the rate.

risks.risk: `source_findings` depends on the problem-string format at pin.rs:489-492. A format change would stop requests from being queued, silently.
risks.mitigation: The parse accepts only that exact shape, and the integration test `source_check_fix_*` runs the real checker path, so a format change fails a test.

risks.risk: Statement text holding a line that starts '- ', '* ' or '1. ', a newline, or a boundary word could make `athena plan` read extra acceptance or admission refuse the text.
risks.mitigation: Every finding line starts with 'Finding N in', whitespace is collapsed to one line, `StewardRequest::new` rewords boundary words and rejects text whose parsed acceptance differs (steward.rs:587), and unit tests cover each form.

demonstrations.method: Two layers. (1) Unit, in drain.rs `mod tests`: a stub `FixStub` implements `Steps`; its `check_page` is the fake source check and returns `Check::fail(..).with_findings(vec![SourceFinding { file: studies/demo/claims.json, kind: contradicted, text: the quoted statement and its evidence }])`. Its `queue_request` stores the text in a `RefCell<Vec<String>>` and `open_requests` returns those texts as `OpenRequest`s (state 'queued'). That is storage only; the code under test is `Drain::rate`, `queue_source_fix`, `steward::source_fix_request` and `steward::citing_request`, and none of it is in the double. Run `drain()` three times on one stub: first drain queues exactly one request; second queues none; a third with the same file and kind but a differently worded statement queues none; a fourth with a finding for another file queues one citing only that finding. Assert the stored text starts with 'Priority: high', holds the statement, its evidence and the marker line, has a non-empty `request_text_acceptance`, and that report.notes names the queued job on the first run and names the citing request and its state on the second. (2) Integration, in tests/drain.rs: `source_check_fix_queues_one_request_then_none_while_it_is_open` runs `drain::drain` over `WithRealCheck` (real `RealSteps::check_page`, `RealSteps::open_requests` and `RealSteps::queue_request`) with the fake checker `judge` and `WRONG_CLAIM` in a `commit_study` repository. After the first drain `Records::load` shows exactly one non-closed request job whose text holds WRONG_CLAIM, the pinned-source evidence and `Source finding: studies/demo/claims.json (contradicted)`. After a second drain with a fresh stub on the same repository it still shows one. The matching rules are also covered by steward.rs unit tests named `source_fix_*`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli source_check_fix && cargo test -p athena-core source_fix
demonstrations.observes: After the first drain exactly one request exists, citing the contradicted statement and its source; after the second, still one; a reworded statement for the same file and kind adds none; a finding for another file adds one that cites only itself. The steward.rs tests show the request is built by `StewardRequest::new`, reads as acceptance bullets, and that a boundary-word or a mid-line '- ' statement is reworded and still builds.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no queueing in `rate()` the store stays empty and the first count assertion fails. With no dedupe the second drain adds a second request. With the statement or evidence in the key the reworded third drain adds a duplicate. If pin.rs changed its problem format, `source_findings` would return nothing and the integration test would see zero requests.
